cards.card: Secured credit card with a term deposit

note: The main banks, chosen as the best-known large card issuers (no central bank ranking was read): Khan Bank, Golomt Bank and the Trade and Development Bank; only the Trade and Development Bank's pages, already found, were read this time, for want of the research's budget. The Trade and Development Bank of Mongolia's four credit card pages, read on 2026-10-30 (the Gold first read 2026-10-29): the Gold and Lady cards cost 19,900 tugriks a year, charge 2% a month on purchases and 3% on cash, give up to 45 days free of interest and ask a minimum payment of 10%; the Platinum costs 299,900 a year, at the same rates, with up to 50 days free and a 10% minimum; the card secured against a term deposit costs 19,900 a year, charges 1.83% a month on purchases in tugriks, gives no interest-free period and asks a 10% minimum (a condition, the pledged deposit, the game doesn't check). Each charges an over-limit fee and a past-due fee of 1%, at least 10,000 tugriks; the pages don't name what the 1% is of, so neither is written. The cards' dollar terms aren't written. Wave 4 (2026-10-30): Golomt Bank, one of the three largest banks, is added from its English card pages; Khan Bank's site didn't answer, XacBank's and the State Bank's carry a captcha (2026-10-30). Golomt Bank's card pages (read 2026-10-30): the Si credit card, 100,000 tugriks a year (50 US dollars for its dollar version, not written), retail interest 2% a month and cash 3% a month, a minimum payment of 10%, up to 50 days free of interest on purchases; the Virtual Credit card (American Express, used through the SocialPay app), 3,000 tugriks a year, 2.0% a month on purchases from the day after the due date and 3.0% on cash, a 10% minimum, up to 45 days free. Each states a monthly late-payment charge of 1% (on the virtual card, 'penalty interest'), which doesn't say whether it replaces or adds to the rate, and isn't written; nor are the Si card's excess-limit charges (5% and 10,000 tugriks a month, the share's base not named) or its ATM fees, whose figures sit in two currency columns that can't be told apart. The Color and UnionPay virtual credit cards' pages weren't read.
